findings.title: Human approver references are not authenticated identities
attack_path: A caller able to invoke the approval path supplies a syntactically valid human reference.
The parser verifies the reference shape but not an external identity or authorization binding.
A benchmarked candidate could be promoted under an impersonated operator claim.
evidence: Actor references must start with human but are stored only as hashes.
The specification states that identity binding is a caller responsibility.
findings.recommendation: Require authenticated operator binding at the host boundary before production use.

findings.title: Gate results and evidence references are caller-supplied
attack_path: A benchmark adapter reports passing checks or permissive thresholds without valid retained executions.
The gate deterministically evaluates the supplied values and records their references.
A human could approve and promote a candidate based on unsupported evidence.
evidence: Prompt 122 records check outcomes but does not execute unit, security, cost, token, latency, or quality tools.
Safe Mode blocks the mutation path but does not authenticate evidence.
findings.recommendation: Bind each production evidence type to independently verifiable run receipts.

findings.title: Closed bounded approval input limits injection and secret retention
findings.affected_component: Approval parser and schema v72 writes
attack_path: A caller submits malformed, oversized, duplicate, secret-like, or stale approval JSON.
Closed parsing, secret scanning, exact assessment hashes, and parameterized SQL reject it.
Accepted rows retain hashes and typed references rather than raw actor or justification text.
evidence: Focused tests cover model identities, secret-like content, stale hashes, exact tradeoffs, and immutable rows.
The CLI reads one bounded JSON object and exposes no shell or network action.
findings.recommendation: Preserve closed schemas, bounded files, and parameterized writes.

findings.title: The change adds no filesystem, network, shell, memory, or skill execution
attack_path: A caller supplies crafted evidence or justification text.
The runtime validates, hashes, and stores bounded data without interpreting it as instructions.
No command, network request, memory write, skill activation, or provider call is created.
evidence: ContinuousQualityGate depends only on SQLite, hashing, validation, and the existing policy registry.
All SQL values are parameterized and tables are immutable.

limitations: Actor references and gate evidence are not cryptographically authenticated.
The gate does not execute tests, security checks, or benchmarks.
Threshold selection remains an upstream governance responsibility.
An approval can be retained before a compare-and-swap promotion retry succeeds.
No production deployment, release, model provider, network, shell, memory, or skill authority is added.
